title: High Strength and Fracture Resistance of Reduced-Activity W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr High-Entropy Alloy for Fusion Energy Applications.

recollection.starting_material: Near-equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloy based on W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr (arc-melted or powder-metallurgy consolidated ingots/bars).
recollection.intervention: Reduced-activation compositional design followed by vacuum arc melting and homogenization; thermomechanical processing (e.g., hot forging/rolling) and aging to promote controlled nanoscale phase separation/precipitation; mechanical testing (tension and fracture) at room and elevated temperatures.
recollection.structure: Dual-phase bcc-dominant microstructure: an A2 (bcc) solid-solution matrix containing nanoscale secondary phases (either A2/B2 modulated domains or C15-type Laves precipitates) with possible Zr-rich nanoparticle dispersions; hierarchical nanoscale–microscale morphology that stabilizes at high temperature.
recollection.mechanism: High strength from refractory-element solid-solution strengthening plus nanoscale precipitate strengthening and work hardening; fracture resistance from ductile-phase toughening, crack deflection/bridging across phase boundaries, and a rising R-curve due to stable microcrack interactions; reduced activation achieved by choosing W, Ta, Ti, V, Zr to minimize long-lived activation products.
recollection.results: Guess: Room-temperature yield strength ~1.1–1.4 GPa with ultimate tensile strength ~1.4–1.8 GPa and tensile ductility ~8–15%; rising R-curve with fracture toughness on the order of ~80–150 MPa√m; retains substantial strength at 800–1000 °C (yield ~0.6–0.8 GPa); microstructure features 5–50 nm precipitates and micrometer-scale grains; hardness ~500–600 HV with limited embrittlement after thermal exposure.

score.note: The recollection correctly mentions arc melting, mechanical testing, a dual-BCC character, and refractory-element solid-solution strengthening. However, it invents homogenization, thermomechanical processing, aging, nanoscale precipitates, tensile/R-curve testing, and crack-bridging mechanisms. The actual structure was a solidification-segregated W-Ta-rich dendritic/Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic two-BCC microstructure. Quantitative guesses are mostly inaccurate, especially fracture toughness (actual ~38 MPa√m, not 80–150), test mode, ductility, and high-temperature conditions.
